name: Restate offers and declare availability changes
summary: When a plant can no longer deliver what its offer says, because a unit trips, turbines ice up, a hydro unit loses flow or a unit comes back from outage, the company must restate the offer in the AESO Energy Trading System as soon as reasonably practicable and give an acceptable operational reason. Plant operators in the gas control rooms, hydro control centre and renewables operations centre call the real-time desk, which decides the restatement type and hours, enters it, checks the effect on dispatches and reserve awards, and logs the timing. The work is fast but happens hundreds of times a month, peaks during cold snaps when the desk is busiest, and late or missing restatements are the most common ISO rule matters reported to the market surveillance administrator.

baseline.org_archetype: An Alberta merchant generator with about thirty offered assets and a 24-hour real-time desk linked by recorded phone lines to plant control rooms.
baseline.notes: Rules as in force in 2019-2022: section 203.3 (2014 version) and section 203.4 (2020 text). Restatements were keyed in the ETS by the desk.

trigger: A plant operator reports a change in what an asset can deliver: a trip, derate, early or late return from outage, turbine faults or icing, or a hydro flow or head limit.
end_state: The offer in the ETS reflects the asset's real capability for every affected hour with a reason recorded, the position is updated, and the restatement has passed the next-day timeliness review (or been self-reported to the MSA).

volume.seasonality: Higher in winter (cold-weather trips, turbine icing) and in spring run-off for hydro; lower in calm summer months.

evidence.note: Organisation file estimate kept: about 20 restatements a day across about thirty assets, most of them wind farm capability changes. Market-wide, section 203.3 produced 114 compliance matters in 2021 (MSA Compliance Review 2021), which shows restatements are frequent but does not give a count.

surge.cause: winter cold snaps with tight supply

evidence.note: Taken from the organisation file: cold snaps raise demand and volatility and cause more trips, derates and restatements; estimate.

steps.name: Plant condition changes
steps.description: A unit trips or is derated, a unit returns from outage early or late, turbines fault or ice up, or a hydro unit loses head or flow; the plant control system or SCADA raises an alarm or the operator sees the change on the console.

evidence.note: Trigger mix follows the organisation file's triggering processes; the split is an estimate.

steps.name: Gas control room sets the new capability
steps.description: The control room operator first stabilises the unit within its safe operating limits, then works out with the shift supervisor how many MW the unit can deliver, from what time and for how long, and phones the real-time desk with the MW, the cause and the expected duration.

error.defect_description: Capability or duration estimate too optimistic, so a second restatement follows.

control.basis: Plant operating procedures: stabilise the unit within safe operating limits under a certificated shift engineer before reporting capability (Alberta pressure equipment and power engineer rules)

evidence.note: Operator practice is an estimate; the requirement for certificated power engineers is noted in the organisation file.

steps.name: Hydro control sets the new capability
steps.description: The hydro control centre operator checks the tripped or limited unit, reservoir and forebay levels, ice or debris on intakes and licence flow limits on SCADA, works out the plant's new MW capability and calls the real-time desk.

error.defect_description: Capability limit misjudged across the cascade.

evidence.note: Hydro control centre practice is an estimate.

steps.name: Operations centre counts available turbines
steps.description: The renewables operations centre operator counts turbines faulted, iced or stopped for high wind, checks substation and collector limits, waits briefly to see whether an icing or high-wind stop persists, and sends the desk the wind farm's new available MW.

error.defect_description: Turbines reset remotely are still counted as unavailable.

evidence.note: ROC practice is an estimate; most turbine faults are remote resets (organisation file driver dd_turbine_faults).

steps.name: Log the change at the desk
steps.description: The real-time trader takes the call or message on the recorded line, notes the time the company became aware, the asset, the MW, the cause and the expected return time in the desk log, because the restatement clock runs from that moment.

error.defect_description: Awareness time not logged, so timeliness cannot be shown later.

evidence.note: Recorded lines and desk logs are common practice; estimate.

steps.name: Decide what must be restated
steps.description: The trader decides whether the change needs an available capability, MW or minimum stable generation restatement, which hours it covers, whether those hours are inside T-2, and whether the cause is an acceptable operational reason rather than a commercial one.

error.defect_description: Wrong restatement type or hours chosen.

next.condition: no restatement allowed or needed (commercial reason, or change shorter than the rule requires)

evidence.note: Restatement types, T-2 and acceptable operational reasons are stated in 203.3 s.2 to s.5; the 3 percent share is an estimate.

steps.name: Write the operational reason
steps.description: The trader picks the reason category and types the operational reason for the restatement in the ETS reason field, for example forced derate on a boiler feed pump or seven turbines iced, as the rule requires for every available capability restatement.

error.defect_description: Reason too vague to show an acceptable operational reason.

control.basis: ISO Rules section 203.3 s.2(3) and s.4(3): submit the reasons for an available capability restatement and for MW restatements within T-2

evidence.note: Reason requirement in 203.3 s.2(3) and s.4(3); times are estimates.

steps.name: Submit the restatement in the ETS
steps.description: The trader enters the new available capability or redistributed MW for each affected hour in the Energy Trading System, which drops the highest priced blocks out of the merit order on a downward restatement and restores the lowest priced blocks first on an upward one.

control.basis: ISO Rules section 203.3 s.2(2) and s.4(2): restate as soon as reasonably practicable; section 203.4 s.5(1): within 20 minutes when an operational deviation lasts 20 minutes or more

evidence.note: Timing obligations in 203.3 and 203.4 s.5(1); merit order effect in 2012-009R; times are estimates.

steps.name: ETS validates the restatement
steps.description: The ETS acknowledges the restatement and checks it, for example that a price change is not inside T-2 and that minimum stable generation still fits the lowest block, and returns a valid or invalid notice.

evidence.note: Validation notices as in 203.1 s.9; the invalid share is an estimate.

steps.name: Correct a rejected restatement
steps.description: The trader reads the rejection reason, corrects the hours, MW or minimum stable generation and resubmits straight away, because the time spent fixing counts against the as-soon-as-practicable requirement.

control.basis: ISO Rules section 203.3 s.2(2) and s.4(2): restate as soon as reasonably practicable; section 203.4 s.5(1): within 20 minutes when an operational deviation lasts 20 minutes or more

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Check dispatch and reserve impact
steps.description: The trader checks whether the asset is currently dispatched above its new capability or holds an operating reserve award for the affected hours, and whether a new dispatch from the AESO should follow from the restated merit order.

next.condition: reserve award or current dispatch cannot be met

evidence.note: Estimate; reserve awards and energy dispatches interact as described in 203.4 s.7.

steps.name: Call the AESO system controller
steps.description: The trader phones the AESO system controller on the recorded line to report that the asset cannot provide its awarded reserve or dispatched energy, gives the MW and expected duration, and notes the controller's instructions.

control.basis: ISO Rules on operating reserve delivery (division 205) and section 201.7 compliance with dispatches

evidence.note: Reserve delivery rules 205.5 and 205.6 drew the largest ISO rule penalties in 2021; the practice of calling is an estimate.

steps.name: AESO replaces the reserve or redispatches
steps.description: The AESO system controller acknowledges the shortfall, replaces the reserve from other providers or standby offers and issues revised dispatches, which the desk then receives in ADaMS.

evidence.note: Standby reserve suppliers have fifteen minutes to get into position (MSA 2009); timing estimated.

steps.name: Update the position for lost or regained MW
steps.description: The trader updates the ETRM position for the MW lost or regained over the affected hours so the hedge book and the day's open position are right, and tells the gas scheduler when a gas unit's burn changes.

error.defect_description: Position left unchanged for later hours.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Adjust the intraday gas nomination
steps.description: The natural gas scheduler revises the unit's intraday nomination on the pipeline portal or sells surplus gas back, so the plant is not left long or short of fuel after the trip or return.

error.defect_description: Nomination change misses the pipeline cycle.

evidence.note: Estimate; gas buyer role from the organisation file.

steps.name: Follow up on the expected return
steps.description: The trader sets a reminder for the expected return time and checks back with the plant then; if the return is earlier or later than first reported, or the cause changes, the trader restates the further hours.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Complete the restatement log
steps.description: The trader completes the restatement log entry with the awareness time, submission time, hours, MW and the reason text, so the gap between the event and the restatement can be shown to the AESO or MSA.

control.basis: Evidence of timeliness for AESO compliance monitoring and MSA self-reports

evidence.note: The MSA compares AESO capability, dispatch and offer data with participant records when judging timeliness.

steps.name: Lead reviews restatements for timeliness
steps.description: Next business morning the real-time desk lead compares the restatement log with the ETS restatement report and plant event times, checking that each restatement was made promptly with an acceptable reason, and flags any that look late or wrong.

control.basis: Company ISO rules compliance programme: daily review of restatements and self-reporting

evidence.note: 91 percent of ISO rules matters in 2021 were self-reported, which implies participants review their own conduct; review cadence and share are estimates.

steps.name: Assess a possible contravention
steps.description: The market compliance officer gathers the plant event log, recorded call, ETS timestamps and reason text for the flagged restatement, decides whether section 203.3 was breached and whether a self-report to the MSA is needed.

evidence.note: Estimate; shares chosen so that about 20 self-reports a year result, consistent with 114 section 203.3 matters across all Alberta participants in 2021 (MSA Compliance Review 2021).

steps.name: File a self-report with the MSA
steps.description: The compliance officer drafts the self-report with the facts, the cause (often a missed call or a busy desk during a trip) and the corrective action, has it approved by the desk director, and submits it to the MSA.

control.basis: MSA Compliance Process (self-reporting of ISO rule contraventions) and AUC Rule 019 specified penalties

evidence.note: Self-report process and penalty basis described in the MSA review and notices; NSP 2021-112 was self-reported 23 days after the event.

steps.name: MSA decides the matter
steps.description: The MSA reviews the self-report with AESO data and issues forbearance, a no-contravention finding or a notice of specified penalty; in 2021, 74 percent of matters ended in forbearance and 16 percent in a penalty.

evidence.note: Outcome shares from the 2021 review; NSP 2021-112 was issued about 2.5 months after the self-report, so the wait range is anchored on that case and is otherwise an estimate.

exceptions.name: Reserve award or dispatch cannot be met
exceptions.description: The asset holds an operating reserve award or is dispatched above its new capability, so the trader calls the AESO system controller, which replaces the reserve or redispatches.

exceptions.name: Return time changes
exceptions.description: The unit comes back earlier or later than reported, or the cause changes, and further hours are restated.

exceptions.name: Late restatement self-reported
exceptions.description: The daily review finds a restatement made too late or with a weak reason; compliance assesses it and self-reports to the MSA, which usually forbears.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the plant event to the completed next-day review
benchmarks.population: Offer restatements at an Alberta generator, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Most of the elapsed time is the wait for the next business-morning review (about 16 hours for a weekday event, up to about 3 days over a weekend); the restatement itself is in the ETS within minutes. Estimate, not a measured figure.

benchmarks.unit: minutes after becoming aware of the change
benchmarks.population: AESO pool assets (ramp rate and other operating constraints)

benchmarks.unit: ISO rules compliance matters addressed, all Alberta participants

evidence.note: Total from Table A1; the split between forbearance and penalties was not read reliably from the PDF, so it is not used.

pain_points.description: Restatements pile up exactly when the desk is busiest: during cold snaps and volatile hours, trips, dispatches and reserve calls arrive together, and late restatements become the most common ISO rule matter.

evidence.note: Section 203.3 had the most matters (114) of any ISO rule section in 2021.

pain_points.description: Capability is relayed by phone from three different control rooms and re-keyed by the trader, so awareness time, MW and reason are recorded twice and can disagree.

evidence.note: Estimate of 2019-2022 practice.

pain_points.description: First estimates of return time are often wrong, so one event produces several restatements.

evidence.note: Estimate.

sources.title: ISO Rules Section 203.1, Offers and Bids for Energy (effective 2013-12-20)
sources.supports: Offers due before 12:00 on the day before the delivery day and no earlier than 7 days before; offer for every settlement interval for source assets of 5 MW or more; prices of at least 0 and under 1,000 CAD/MWh; block MW, flexible or inflexible flag and minimum stable generation; top block equals maximum capability; available capability equal to maximum capability unless an acceptable operational reason is given; ramp rate and initial start-up time; standing submissions; ETS acknowledgement and valid or invalid notice.

sources.title: Information Document 2012-008R, Energy Offers and Bids (posted 2017-04-04)
sources.supports: Offers have up to seven operating blocks; inflexible blocks dispatched only in full; net-to-grid offers for sites with on-site load; AESO expects operating constraints such as ramp rate to be updated within 15 minutes of becoming aware of a change; constraints are used to judge compliance.

sources.title: ISO Rules Section 203.3, Energy Restatements (effective 2014-07-02)
sources.supports: Available capability restatements only for an acceptable operational reason, an operational deviation or testing, submitted as soon as reasonably practicable with reasons; price and MW restatements allowed only before two hours ahead of the settlement interval (T-2); MW restatements within T-2 require reasons; minimum stable generation restatements. In force through the 2019-2022 period (replaced 2024-04-01).

sources.title: Information Document 2012-009R, Restatements (posted 2017-05-11)
sources.supports: How the Energy Trading System removes the highest priced blocks from the merit order when available capability is restated down and restores the lowest priced blocks first when restated up; price restatements need no operational reason but must be made before T-2 (for HE12, before 9:00); MW restatements keep block prices.

sources.title: ISO Rules Section 203.4, Delivery Requirements for Energy (2023-03-31 administrative version; substantive text from 2020-09-16)
sources.supports: Respond to dispatches with reasonable dispatch protocols, personnel and software; start moving toward the dispatched MW within 10 minutes of the dispatch time; reach steady state within the ramp time plus 40 percent (at least 5 minutes) plus 10 minutes; stay inside the allowable dispatch variance over 10-minute periods; restate within 20 minutes if an operational deviation lasts 20 minutes or longer. The revision history shows the 2023 version only aligned drafting with the 2020 text.

sources.title: Operating Reserves Procurement: Understanding Market Outcomes (2009-09-16)
sources.supports: Watt-Ex day-ahead trading from 9:00 with closes at 9:40 (active regulating), 9:50 (spinning), 10:00 (supplemental), 10:10 to 10:30 (standby products), with over-the-counter trades after close; typical procured volumes (about 110 to 165 MW regulating, 170 to 260 MW spinning and supplemental); standby suppliers have fifteen minutes to get into position.

sources.title: MSA Compliance Review 2021 (April 5, 2022)
sources.supports: 462 ISO rules matters addressed in 2021 (437 in 2020), 91 percent self-reported; 75 notices of specified penalty totalling 129,250 CAD; 114 matters under section 203.3 (restatements), 83 under 203.4 (dispatch delivery), 67 under 201.7 (dispatch acknowledgement), 43 under 205.6 and 26 under 205.5 (reserves); 74 percent of matters closed with forbearance; TransAlta entities among those penalised.

sources.title: Notice of Specified Penalty, MSA file 2021-112 (section 203.3, available capability not restated after a trip)
sources.supports: A trip on February 16, 2021 left available capability unrestated for HE12 to HE14; self-reported on March 11, 2021; 750 CAD penalty for a first contravention in 12 months; the MSA relies on AESO available capability, dispatch, generation and offer data.

assumptions: One case is one restatement event for one asset, which may cover several hours. Follow-up restatements for the same event loop back inside the case (15 percent).

The trigger mix (15 percent forced outages, 15 percent start-stop and returns, 40 percent wind, 30 percent hydro) is an estimate; wind farms restate most often because turbine availability changes many times a day.
The volume of 600 a month is the organisation file's estimate and is the number most worth checking against ETS data.

The share that ends in a self-report (about 0.3 percent, about 20 a year) is scaled from the 114 section 203.3 matters across all Alberta participants in 2021, assuming this company holds roughly a sixth of that activity.
The MSA disposition wait is long (months) but rare, so it shows in the cycle time only beyond the 99th percentile.
The surge copies the organisation file's cold-snap surge.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file (wage x 1.40).
